requirements.title: Feature switch and static validation of [sandbox]
requirements.rationale: An operator who mistypes a key must learn of every mistake in one start, and a hub without the section must behave as if sandboxes did not exist.

criteria.condition: the configuration is loaded and the file has no [sandbox] section
criteria.action: report sandboxes as off, build no runtime client, and let the hub start without contacting any gateway and without changing stored sandbox records
criteria.contract: the loaded sandbox configuration reports enabled == false; the hub reaches 'listening'; the runtime factory is never called; GET /version has no sandbox_runtime member

setup: a hub composed with a counting runtime factory
check.pseudocode: in internal/sandbox/config_test.go and internal/hub/hub_test.go: cfg = load(file without [sandbox]); assert sandbox.FromConfig(cfg).Enabled == false; start a hub with a runtime factory that counts its calls; assert the hub listens; assert factoryCalls == 0; assert 'sandbox_runtime' not in get('/version').json

criteria.condition: the configuration is loaded and its [sandbox] section sets only gateway_url, one way to authenticate and one profile with name and ttl, with [server].external_url set
criteria.action: accept the section and fill every other key with its default
criteria.contract: enabled == true; runtime 'openshell'; openshell_workspace 'parley'; max_ttl 24h; idle_timeout 30m; max_sandboxes 200; max_per_org 100; max_per_workspace 50; max_per_user 20; allow_workspace_rules true; max_exec_timeout 30m; max_concurrent_execs 8; max_transfer_size 1073741824 bytes; log_retention 168h; reconcile_interval 1m; no credentials; a file value replaces its default, and ${NAME} references in string values are replaced before validation

setup: a configuration file whose [sandbox] section has gateway_url https://gw.test:8443, a readable non-empty token_file, [server].external_url set, and one profile {name 'agent', ttl '4h'}
check.pseudocode: in internal/sandbox/config_test.go: s = loadSandbox(minimal file); assert each field equals the default listed in the contract; s2 = loadSandbox(file setting max_sandboxes = 10, reconcile_interval = '10s', gateway_url = '${GW}' with GW set); assert s2.MaxSandboxes == 10; assert s2.ReconcileInterval == 10s; assert s2.GatewayURL == value of GW

criteria.condition: the [sandbox] section holds one or more invalid values among: runtime other than 'openshell'; gateway_url missing, not a URL, http to a host that is not localhost, 127.0.0.0/8 or ::1, or with user information, a query, a fragment or a path other than '/'; openshell_workspace not matching ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,62}$; max_ttl, max_exec_timeout or log_retention of 0 or less; idle_timeout below 0; max_sandboxes, max_per_org, max_per_workspace, max_per_user or max_concurrent_execs below 1; max_transfer_size not a size; reconcile_interval below 10s or above 10m; a value of the wrong type; a tls_cert, tls_key, tls_ca, token_file or oidc_client_secret_file that cannot be read; a token_file or oidc_client_secret_file that is empty after trimming white space
criteria.action: refuse the whole configuration and report every failure of the section together, each naming its key as sandbox.<key>
criteria.contract: the load returns no configuration and one error whose text contains sandbox.<key> for every invalid key of the case, the failures separated by '; '; with three invalid keys the text names all three; parleyd exits with status 1 and one error line on stderr and writes no 'listening' line; reconcile_interval of exactly 10s and exactly 10m, and http://127.0.0.1:8080 and http://localhost:8080 as gateway_url, are accepted

setup: a configuration file whose [sandbox] section has gateway_url https://gw.test:8443, a readable non-empty token_file, [server].external_url set, and one profile {name 'agent', ttl '4h'}
check.pseudocode: in internal/sandbox/config_test.go, a table with one row per invalid value named in the condition plus the boundary rows of the contract: err = loadSandbox(valid file with the row's change); assert err contains 'sandbox.' + row.key (or err == nil for a boundary row); one more row sets runtime = 'docker', max_ttl = '0s' and reconcile_interval = '5s' together: assert err contains 'sandbox.runtime' and 'sandbox.max_ttl' and 'sandbox.reconcile_interval'

criteria.condition: the [sandbox] section, a [[sandbox.profiles]] table or a [[sandbox.credentials]] table holds a key that is not defined for it
criteria.action: report the unknown key as a failure together with every other failure of the section
criteria.contract: the load returns no configuration and an error containing sandbox.<key>, sandbox.profiles[<name>].<key> or sandbox.credentials[<name>].<key> for the unknown key; when the same file also has an invalid value, the error names both

setup: a configuration file whose [sandbox] section has gateway_url https://gw.test:8443, a readable non-empty token_file, [server].external_url set, and one profile {name 'agent', ttl '4h'}
check.pseudocode: in internal/sandbox/config_test.go, a table over {sandbox.gatway_url, sandbox.profiles[agent].imge, sandbox.credentials[model].secrt}: err = loadSandbox(valid file plus the misspelled key); assert err contains row.name; one row adds max_ttl = '0s' as well: assert err contains both names

criteria.condition: the section configures no way to authenticate to the gateway, or more than one of mutual TLS (tls_cert with tls_key), token_file and OIDC client credentials, or only one of tls_cert and tls_key, or one or two of oidc_issuer, oidc_client_id and oidc_client_secret_file
criteria.action: refuse the configuration with a failure that names the keys concerned
criteria.contract: the error contains sandbox.gateway_url and the list of ways found (none, or for example 'mutual TLS, token_file') when the count of ways is not one; it contains sandbox.tls_cert or sandbox.tls_key for an incomplete pair and the missing sandbox.oidc_… keys for an incomplete triple; tls_ca together with exactly one way is accepted

setup: a configuration file whose [sandbox] section has gateway_url https://gw.test:8443, a readable non-empty token_file, [server].external_url set, and one profile {name 'agent', ttl '4h'}, with the files of every row present in t.TempDir()
check.pseudocode: in internal/sandbox/config_test.go, a table over {no auth, token_file + tls pair, token_file + oidc triple, tls_cert alone, tls_key alone, oidc_issuer alone, issuer + client_id, token_file + tls_ca (valid), tls pair + tls_ca (valid)}: err = loadSandbox(row); assert err contains every key the row expects, or err == nil for the valid rows

criteria.action: for any [sandbox] section that fails validation, produce a message that contains neither the content of token_file, nor the content of oidc_client_secret_file, nor the user information of a URL value
criteria.contract: the error text of a failing load contains none of: the token file's content, the client secret file's content, the text between '://' and '@' of gateway_url or oidc_issuer

check.pseudocode: in internal/sandbox/config_test.go, a table over failing files that also carry a token file with content 'tok-SECRET-1', a secret file with content 'oidc-SECRET-2' and gateway_url 'https://u:pw-SECRET-3@gw.test': err = loadSandbox(row); assert err != nil; assert err contains none of 'tok-SECRET-1', 'oidc-SECRET-2', 'pw-SECRET-3'

criteria.condition: the file has a [sandbox] section and [server].external_url is empty
criteria.action: refuse the configuration with a failure that names server.external_url, reported together with the other failures of the section
criteria.contract: the load returns no configuration and an error containing server.external_url; the same file without the [sandbox] section loads

check.pseudocode: in internal/sandbox/config_test.go: err = load(valid sandbox file with external_url removed); assert err contains 'server.external_url'; assert load(same file without [sandbox]) succeeds

criteria.condition: the file sets max_per_org above max_sandboxes
criteria.action: refuse the configuration with a failure that names sandbox.max_per_org; when the file does not set max_per_org, use the smaller of 100 and max_sandboxes instead of failing
criteria.contract: max_sandboxes = 50 with max_per_org = 60 fails with an error containing sandbox.max_per_org; max_sandboxes = 50 alone loads with max_per_org == 50; max_sandboxes = 50 with max_per_org = 50 loads; max_sandboxes = 500 alone loads with max_per_org == 100

check.pseudocode: in internal/sandbox/config_test.go, a table over the four cases of the contract: s, err = loadSandbox(row); assert the row's error or the row's MaxPerOrg

requirements.title: Profiles and configured credentials
requirements.rationale: Agents get sandboxes only of shapes the operator declared, so a profile that is wrong must never reach a running hub.

criteria.condition: a valid [sandbox] section is loaded
criteria.action: make each profile available by name with its defaults filled in, the default profile available on request, and all profiles listable in name order, unchanged for the life of the process
criteria.contract: a profile that sets only name and ttl has default false, description '', image '', cpu '', memory '', gpu 0, idle_timeout equal to [sandbox].idle_timeout, no policy file (the built-in policy), credentials [], optional_credentials [], expose_secrets [], optional_expose_secrets [], hub_access 'fork', env {}, checkpoint true, allow_proposals true; lookup of an unknown name reports 'no such profile' as a result; the default lookup reports 'no default' when no profile sets default; the list is sorted by name; each configured credential is available by name with provider_profile and secret

check.pseudocode: in internal/sandbox/profile_test.go: s = loadSandbox(file with profiles 'b' {ttl 1h}, 'a' {ttl 2h, default true, idle_timeout '0s', credentials ['model']} and credential model); assert names(s.Profiles()) == ['a','b']; assert s.Profile('b') has every default of the contract; assert s.Profile('a').IdleTimeout == 0; assert s.DefaultProfile().Name == 'a'; assert s.Profile('zz') not found; assert s.Credential('model') == {provider_profile, secret}; with no default set: assert s.DefaultProfile() reports none

criteria.condition: the section has no profile, or a profile has: no name or a name not matching ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,62}$; a name another profile has; default true while another profile sets it; no ttl, a ttl of 0 or less, or a ttl above [sandbox].max_ttl; an idle_timeout below 0; a gpu below 0; a hub_access other than 'fork' and 'none'; a policy file that cannot be read
criteria.action: refuse the configuration and report each failure with the key sandbox.profiles[<name>].<key>, using the profile's zero-based index when it has no usable name, together with every other failure of the section
criteria.contract: the error contains sandbox.profiles for a section without profiles and sandbox.profiles[<name or index>].<key> for each failing field; a name of 63 characters and a ttl equal to max_ttl are accepted; a name of 64 characters and a ttl one second above max_ttl are refused; two profiles with default true are refused with an error naming the second one's default

check.pseudocode: in internal/sandbox/profile_test.go, a table with one row per failure named in the condition and the four boundary rows of the contract: err = loadSandbox(valid file with the row's change); assert err contains row.key, or err == nil for an accepted boundary; one row breaks ttl of profile 'a' and hub_access of profile 'b': assert err contains 'sandbox.profiles[a].ttl' and 'sandbox.profiles[b].hub_access'

criteria.condition: a [[sandbox.credentials]] entry has no name, a name not matching ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,62}$, a name another entry has, an empty provider_profile or an empty secret; or a profile's credentials or optional_credentials names an entry that does not exist; or one name is in both of a profile's two credential lists
criteria.action: refuse the configuration and report each failure with its key
criteria.contract: the error contains sandbox.credentials[<name or index>].<key> for a failing entry, and sandbox.profiles[<name>].credentials or sandbox.profiles[<name>].optional_credentials together with the offending credential name for a failing reference

check.pseudocode: in internal/sandbox/profile_test.go, a table over {entry without name, name 'Bad Name', duplicate name, provider_profile '', secret '', profile references 'nope' in credentials, in optional_credentials, 'model' in both lists}: err = loadSandbox(row); assert err contains row.key and, for a reference row, the credential name

criteria.condition: a key of a profile's env does not match ^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$ or starts with PARLEY_ or OPENSHELL_
criteria.action: refuse the configuration with a failure naming sandbox.profiles[<name>].env and the key
criteria.contract: the error contains sandbox.profiles[<name>].env and the offending key; the keys PARLEYX, parley_lower and _X are accepted; the error text does not contain the value of the entry

check.pseudocode: in internal/sandbox/profile_test.go, a table over env keys {'PARLEY_X', 'OPENSHELL_Y', '1ABC', 'A-B', '' (refused); 'PARLEYX', 'parley_lower', '_X' (accepted)} each with value 'val-SECRETISH': err = loadSandbox(row); refused rows: assert err contains 'sandbox.profiles[agent].env' and the key and not 'val-SECRETISH'; accepted rows: assert err == nil

criteria.condition: a name in a profile's expose_secrets or optional_expose_secrets does not match ^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$, starts with PARLEY_ or OPENSHELL_, equals without regard to case one of GIT_PAT, GIT_USERNAME, GIT_PASSWORD, UPSTREAM_GIT_PAT, UPSTREAM_GIT_USERNAME, UPSTREAM_GIT_PASSWORD or FORGE_WEBHOOK_SECRET, is a key of the profile's env, or is in both lists
criteria.action: refuse the configuration with a failure naming the profile's list key and the name, without checking whether any secret exists
criteria.contract: the error contains sandbox.profiles[<name>].expose_secrets or sandbox.profiles[<name>].optional_expose_secrets and the offending name; a profile with expose_secrets ['NPM_TOKEN'] and optional_expose_secrets ['PIP_TOKEN'] loads although no such secret is stored

check.pseudocode: in internal/sandbox/profile_test.go, a table over {'1TOKEN', 'A-B', 'PARLEY_TOKEN', 'OPENSHELL_X', 'GIT_PAT', 'git_pat', 'FORGE_WEBHOOK_SECRET', a name that is also an env key, a name in both lists} for each of the two lists: err = loadSandbox(row); assert err contains the list key and the name; the valid row of the contract: assert err == nil

requirements.title: Start-up runtime check
requirements.rationale: A hub that starts against a gateway it cannot use would accept sandbox requests it can never serve.

criteria.condition: parleyd starts with a valid [sandbox] section and the runtime accepts every step
criteria.action: before binding the listener and exactly once, authenticate and read the gateway's release, check the release against the supported range, make sure the configured OpenShell workspace exists, install the provider profile 'parley-hub', read every provider_profile named in [[sandbox.credentials]], and send every profile's policy file for validation, in that order, and then mark the runtime reachable
criteria.contract: the runtime received the calls in the order release, ensure workspace(openshell_workspace), install provider profile(id 'parley-hub', variable PARLEY_API_KEY, the scheme, host and port of [server].external_url, path prefixes /api/v1/ and /git/), get provider profile (once per distinct provider_profile), validate policy (once per profile that names a policy file, none for the built-in policy); the hub then writes its 'listening' line; Reachable() is true; a second start against the same runtime leaves one 'parley-hub' profile and one workspace

setup: a runtime fake reporting a release inside the supported range and holding the provider profile 'anthropic' with declared variable ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
a configuration with credential model -> anthropic, profile 'agent' with a policy file and profile 'plain' without one
check.pseudocode: in internal/sandbox/startcheck_test.go: rt = fake; err = startcheck.Run(ctx, cfg, rt); assert err == nil; assert kinds(rt.Calls()) == ['release','ensure_workspace','install_provider_profile','get_provider_profile','validate_policy']; assert rt.ProviderProfile('parley-hub').Variables == ['PARLEY_API_KEY'] and its host == host of external_url; assert rt.Workspaces() == ['parley']; assert client.Reachable(); run again: assert count of 'parley-hub' == 1; in internal/hub/hub_test.go: a hub started with this fake logs 'listening' only after the last call

criteria.condition: the gateway cannot be reached, refuses the hub's credential, or answers the first call with a failure of kind unavailable
criteria.action: stop the check at that step, make no later call, and fail the start with a message that names sandbox.gateway_url
criteria.contract: parleyd exits with status 1; stderr holds exactly one line and it contains sandbox.gateway_url; no 'listening' line is written; the line contains neither the gateway token nor the OIDC client secret; the workspace was not created and no provider profile was installed

setup: a token_file whose content is 'gw-tok-SECRET'
check.pseudocode: in internal/sandbox/startcheck_test.go, a table over {fake set unreachable, fake failing 'release' as unavailable with text containing the token}: err = startcheck.Run(ctx, cfg, rt); assert err contains 'sandbox.gateway_url'; assert err does not contain the token; assert rt.Calls() has only 'release'; in internal/hub/hub_test.go: status, stderr = runHub(cfg, factory returning that fake); assert status == 1; assert lines(stderr) == 1; assert 'listening' not in stderr

criteria.condition: the gateway's release is below the lowest supported release, at or above the first unsupported release, or not a semantic version
criteria.action: fail the start with a message that holds the connected release and the supported range, without creating the workspace or installing anything
criteria.contract: the error contains the release the gateway reported and the range text '>=<lowest> <<first unsupported>'; the only call made is the release read; a release equal to the lowest supported one is accepted and one equal to the first unsupported one is refused

setup: a runtime fake reporting a release inside the supported range and holding the provider profile 'anthropic' with declared variable ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
check.pseudocode: in internal/sandbox/compat_test.go and startcheck_test.go, with the range {1.2.0, 2.0.0} injected, a table over releases {'1.1.9' refuse, '1.2.0' accept, '1.9.3' accept, '2.0.0' refuse, 'v1.4.0' accept, 'nightly' refuse, '' refuse}: rt.SetRelease(row); err = startcheck.Run(ctx, cfg, rt); refused: assert err contains row.release (when not empty) and '>=1.2.0 <2.0.0'; assert rt.Calls() == ['release']; accepted: assert err == nil

criteria.condition: a provider_profile named in [[sandbox.credentials]] is not known to the gateway
criteria.action: fail the start with a message that names sandbox.credentials[<name>].provider_profile and the profile id
criteria.contract: the error contains sandbox.credentials[<name>].provider_profile and the missing id; no policy file was sent for validation

setup: a runtime fake reporting a release inside the supported range and holding the provider profile 'anthropic' with declared variable ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
check.pseudocode: in internal/sandbox/startcheck_test.go: cfg has credential 'model' -> provider_profile 'missing'; err = startcheck.Run(ctx, cfg, rt); assert err contains 'sandbox.credentials[model].provider_profile' and 'missing'; assert 'validate_policy' not in kinds(rt.Calls())

criteria.condition: the runtime rejects a profile's policy file, or reports that it has no operation to validate one
criteria.action: fail the start with a message that names sandbox.profiles[<name>].policy and carries the runtime's reason, scrubbed
criteria.contract: the error contains sandbox.profiles[<name>].policy; for a rejection it contains the runtime's reason text; a configuration whose profiles all use the built-in policy starts against a runtime without the validation operation

setup: a runtime fake reporting a release inside the supported range and holding the provider profile 'anthropic' with declared variable ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
check.pseudocode: in internal/sandbox/startcheck_test.go, a table over {fake rejects the policy with reason 'unknown field egress', fake fails 'validate_policy' as unsupported}: err = startcheck.Run(ctx, cfg, rt); assert err contains 'sandbox.profiles[agent].policy'; rejection row: assert err contains 'unknown field egress'; third row: cfg without any policy file and the fake failing 'validate_policy' as unsupported: assert err == nil

criteria.condition: a name in a profile's expose_secrets or optional_expose_secrets equals a variable declared by the provider profile of one of that profile's credentials or optional_credentials
criteria.action: fail the start with a message that names the profile and the name
criteria.contract: the error contains sandbox.profiles[<name>].expose_secrets or sandbox.profiles[<name>].optional_expose_secrets and the variable's name; the same name exposed by a profile that does not attach that credential is accepted

setup: a runtime fake reporting a release inside the supported range and holding the provider profile 'anthropic' with declared variable ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
check.pseudocode: in internal/sandbox/startcheck_test.go, a table over {profile 'agent' with credentials ['model'] and expose_secrets ['ANTHROPIC_API_KEY'], the same through optional_credentials and optional_expose_secrets, profile 'other' without the credential exposing ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (accepted)}: err = startcheck.Run(ctx, cfg, rt); assert err contains the list key and 'ANTHROPIC_API_KEY', or err == nil for the accepted row

criteria.condition: the runtime check has not finished 30 seconds after it began
criteria.action: abandon the check and fail the start with a message that names sandbox.gateway_url and says that the runtime did not answer in time
criteria.contract: every call of the check carries a context whose deadline is at most 30 seconds after the check began; when a call blocks until that deadline the check returns an error containing sandbox.gateway_url, and parleyd exits with status 1 without a 'listening' line

setup: a runtime fake reporting a release inside the supported range and holding the provider profile 'anthropic' with declared variable ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
check.pseudocode: in internal/sandbox/startcheck_test.go: the fake's 'ensure_workspace' blocks until its context ends and records the context's deadline; run startcheck with the production budget on a clock the test controls (or with a budget of 50 ms for the blocking run): assert err contains 'sandbox.gateway_url'; assert recordedDeadline - start <= 30s

criteria.condition: sandboxes are on and the start-up check has succeeded
criteria.action: include in the document of GET /version the member sandbox_runtime with the supported range and the release read from the gateway at start
criteria.contract: GET /version answers 200 with sandbox_runtime == {"supported": ">=<lowest> <<first unsupported>", "connected": "<release>"} beside the members it has without sandboxes; the member stays the same while the runtime is unreachable

setup: a runtime fake reporting a release inside the supported range and holding the provider profile 'anthropic' with declared variable ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
check.pseudocode: in internal/hub/hub_test.go: start a hub with the fake reporting release '1.4.2' and the range {1.2.0, 2.0.0}; v = get('/version').json; assert v.sandbox_runtime == {supported: '>=1.2.0 <2.0.0', connected: '1.4.2'}; assert v.version != ''; rt.SetUnreachable(true); assert get('/version').json.sandbox_runtime.connected == '1.4.2'

requirements.title: Runtime client
requirements.rationale: Packages 45 to 48 drive sandboxes through one client, so its scope, its error kinds and its test double must be fixed before they are written.

criteria.action: for any operation of the client interface (gateway, provider profiles, providers, policy, sandboxes, exec, files, logs), act in the configured OpenShell workspace and in no other
criteria.contract: a sandbox, provider or provider profile created through the client exists in the workspace named by openshell_workspace and is not visible to a client configured with another workspace; a sandbox list returns only sandboxes of the configured workspace

setup: the OpenShell implementation over the SDK's in-memory fake client, and the fake of this package, each as one backend shared by two clients
check.pseudocode: in internal/sandbox/runtime/runtimetest/contract.go, run by internal/sandbox/runtime/openshell/client_test.go and runtimetest/fake_test.go: a = client(workspace 'parley'); b = client(workspace 'other') over the same backend; id = a.CreateSandbox(spec); assert a.GetSandbox(id) found; assert kind(b.GetSandbox(id)) == not found; assert ids(b.ListSandboxes()) == []; a.EnsureProvider('p', 'anthropic', 'v'); assert kind(b.DeleteProvider('p')) == not found

criteria.condition: an operation fails
criteria.action: return an error of exactly one of four kinds that a caller can test for: not found when the runtime has no such sandbox, provider, provider profile, proposal or path; invalid when the runtime understood and refused the request, keeping the runtime's reason; unsupported when the SDK in use has no such operation; unavailable for every other failure, including a gateway that cannot be reached, a refused hub credential and a server error of the gateway
criteria.contract: errors.Is(err, runtime.ErrNotFound), ErrInvalid, ErrUnsupported or ErrUnavailable is true for exactly one of the four; an invalid error's text contains the runtime's reason; every operation the SDK has no call for (StopSandbox, StartSandbox, ValidatePolicy, AddPolicyRule, RunMain, Stat, MakeDir and Walk are the candidates) returns ErrUnsupported and is never imitated with other calls

check.pseudocode: in internal/sandbox/runtime/openshell/errors_test.go and runtimetest/contract.go, a table over {get of an unknown sandbox -> not found, delete of an unknown provider -> not found, get of an unknown provider profile -> not found, Stat of a missing path -> not found, validate of a policy the backend rejects with reason 'bad rule' -> invalid and text contains 'bad rule', create with an image reference the backend refuses -> invalid, backend connection refused -> unavailable, backend answers unauthenticated -> unavailable, backend answers a server error -> unavailable, an operation the backend lacks -> unsupported}: err = op(); assert exactly one of the four errors.Is holds and it is the row's

criteria.condition: an operation ends
criteria.action: clear the reachability flag when it ended with kind unavailable and set it when it ended in any other way, a success and the kinds not found, invalid and unsupported included, and report every change of the flag to the metrics recorder
criteria.contract: Reachable() is false after an unavailable result and true after the next result of any other kind; it is safe to read while operations run in other goroutines; the hub process does not exit on any result; the recorder received parley_sandbox_runtime_up 0 when the flag was cleared and 1 when it was set again, once per change

check.pseudocode: in internal/sandbox/runtime/runtimetest/contract.go: c.GetSandbox('none'); assert c.Reachable() (not found counts as reachable); backend.SetUnreachable(true); c.ListSandboxes(); assert !c.Reachable(); backend.SetUnreachable(false); c.Release(); assert c.Reachable(); in internal/sandbox/runtime/openshell/client_test.go with a recording recorder: assert its calls == [Set(parley_sandbox_runtime_up, 0), Set(parley_sandbox_runtime_up, 1)]; run 50 goroutines calling operations while another reads Reachable() under the race detector

criteria.condition: an operation that does not stream has not returned 30 seconds after it was called, or the caller's context ends sooner
criteria.action: stop waiting and return an error of kind unavailable
criteria.contract: the call returns within the smaller of 30 seconds and the caller's deadline, with errors.Is(err, runtime.ErrUnavailable); WatchSandboxes, followed Logs, ExecStream, ExecInteractive, Upload, Download and Walk are not bound by the 30 seconds and end when the caller's context ends

check.pseudocode: in internal/sandbox/runtime/openshell/client_test.go: the backend blocks GetSandbox until its context ends and records the deadline; with a caller context of 50 ms: err = c.GetSandbox(ctx, id); assert kind(err) == unavailable; assert elapsed < 1s; with a background context: assert recordedDeadline - callTime <= 30s; for a followed log read with a background context: assert the backend's context has no deadline; cancel the caller's context: assert the stream ends

criteria.condition: the client is built from a valid [sandbox] section
criteria.action: connect to gateway_url with the one configured way to authenticate: the client certificate and key for mutual TLS, the trimmed content of token_file as a static bearer token, or a token obtained and renewed with the OIDC client credentials; and trust tls_ca for the gateway's certificate when it is set
criteria.contract: the SDK configuration built for a mutual-TLS section carries the client certificate and no token source; for token_file it carries a static token equal to the file's content without surrounding white space; for OIDC it carries a renewing token source built from oidc_issuer, oidc_client_id and the content of oidc_client_secret_file; Address is gateway_url's host and port; with tls_ca the TLS settings trust that CA only

setup: a self-signed certificate, key and CA written to t.TempDir()
check.pseudocode: in internal/sandbox/runtime/openshell/config_test.go, a table over {mutual TLS, token_file with content ' tok\n', OIDC, token_file + tls_ca}: sdkCfg = openshell.BuildConfig(section); assert sdkCfg.Address == 'gw.test:8443'; assert the row's Auth and TLS members as in the contract

real_components: hub start sequence and start hooks
HTTP router with authentication, scope check and workspace access
setup: a hub started in-process with sandboxes on over the SDK's in-memory fake client
an in-memory sandbox source holding one sandbox object
a test-only route of kind read on a workspace the developer owns, whose handler returns the error of a runtime get
the SDK fake is switched to refuse connections after the start
end_state: GET /api/v1/sandboxes with the admin token answers 200 with the one stored object
the test-only route answers 502 with error_type sandbox_runtime_error
the runtime client reports Reachable() == false
smoke.pseudocode: in test/e2e/sandbox_runtime_test.go: hub = startHub(cfg, runtimeFactory(sdkFake), source, probe); sdkFake.refuseConnections(); r = get(probe, developerKey); assert r.status == 502 and r.json.error.error_type == 'sandbox_runtime_error'; assert !hub.Runtime().Reachable(); assert len(get('/api/v1/sandboxes', admin).json.items) == 1; assert get('/api/v1/sandbox-profiles', developerKey).status == 200; assert get('/healthz').status == 200
